source.source: HYG v4.4 (Hipparcos-Yale-Gliese Database, D. Nash / astronexus)

source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Itokawa pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: Pinned JPL Horizons heliocentric elements and the source mission body-fixed rotation model
provenance.qualification: Computed Itokawa Sun direction at 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose.

controls.label: AMICA mosaic
controls.description: Seven Hayabusa AMICA v-band images from September and October 2005, including closer views from north of the equator, are registered with the archived Gaskell Cartesian backplanes. Grayscale shows flat-fielded detector brightness with approximate illumination correction and bounded overlap matching, not absolute albedo or natural color. The source images use lossy 8-bit compression; photographed shadows and some seams remain. The ordinary grid marks missing, grazing or geometrically rejected coverage.
controls.summary: Brightness is corrected and matched across seven images. Shadows and seams remain; the grid marks gaps and rejected coverage.
controls.title: AMICA v-band mosaic

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: Color shows radius minus a 165 m reference sphere, including the body's broad irregular shape. This is not gravitational height or an image observation. Brightness adds cartographic relief from the full source model; Shadows adds approximate fixed-epoch Sun lighting. Fine terrain is represented in the map while the displayed silhouette is simplified. Values follow the nearest corresponding point on the full source shape within the display mesh’s simplification allowance. This is radial height, not gravitational height; flat previews withhold overlapping radial surfaces.
controls.summary: Height relative to a 165 m sphere, from the shape model. Colors include the broad form; the outline is simplified.
controls.title: Shape-derived radial height
